title: Scheduled scenario does not run at expected time
problem: A Make scenario set to run on a schedule does not execute at the expected time or misses scheduled runs.
symptoms: Scenario execution history shows gaps where expected scheduled runs did not occur
Scenario is active but has not run for a longer time than the configured schedule
Scheduled run is delayed compared to the configured time

likely_causes.cause: The scenario is inactive — scheduled scenarios only run when the scenario is active
The operations quota was exhausted, preventing scheduled executions from starting
Make experienced a platform-level delay or incident affecting scheduled scenario execution
The scenario's scheduling configuration was not saved correctly after the last change

diagnosis_steps: Verify that the scenario is active — the toggle must be ON
Check Make Dashboard > Usage to confirm the operations quota is not exhausted
Check Make's status page for any recent platform incidents that may have affected scheduling
Open the scenario's scheduling configuration and verify the schedule is set correctly (correct time zone, interval, specific days if configured)
Check the execution history for any error on the last attempted run

solutions.solution: Activate the scenario if it was inactive
solutions.conditions: When the scenario was deactivated — the most common cause

solutions.solution: Resolve the operations quota issue (upgrade plan or pause non-critical scenarios) to allow scheduled runs to resume
solutions.conditions: When the operations quota was exhausted

solutions.solution: Review and resave the scheduling configuration, paying attention to time zone settings
solutions.conditions: When the schedule appears configured but runs do not occur at the expected time

prevention: Set up scenario failure notifications to detect when scheduled scenarios stop running
Monitor operations quota usage to prevent exhaustion from stopping scheduled scenarios

origin_details.evidence: Make scheduling requires scenario to be active. Operations quota affects all executions including scheduled ones.

audit_notes: Scenario must be active for scheduling to work is confirmed in Make documentation. Operations quota blocking scheduled runs is a confirmed Make behavior. Platform delays are possible but not documented as a specific scenario type.

evidence.claim: Make scheduling requires scenario to be active. Operations quota affects all executions including scheduled ones.

diagnostic_signals: Scenario execution history shows gaps where expected scheduled runs did not occur
Scenario is active but has not run for a longer time than the configured schedule
Scheduled run is delayed compared to the configured time

title: Scheduled scenario runs at wrong time — time zone mismatch
problem: A Make scenario is configured to run at a specific time but executes at a different clock time. The discrepancy is caused by a mismatch between the time zone configured in Make's scheduling and the expected local time.
symptoms: Scenario runs at a consistent but unexpected time (e.g., 2 hours earlier or later than expected)
The time offset corresponds to a time zone difference
The discrepancy changes during daylight saving time transitions

likely_causes.cause: The scheduling time zone in Make is set to a different zone than the intended local time zone
Daylight saving time transition caused a one-hour shift in the effective run time

diagnosis_steps: Check the time zone setting in the schedule
Compare the configured time zone with the intended local time zone
Calculate the offset between the configured time zone and the expected execution time

solutions.solution: Update the scheduling time zone to the correct local time zone, or adjust the scheduled time to account for the offset
solutions.conditions: When the wrong time zone was selected during configuration

prevention: Always explicitly set the time zone in scheduling configuration — do not rely on defaults
Document the intended time zone for each scheduled scenario

origin_details.evidence: Make scheduling allows time zone selection — confirmed in Make documentation.

audit_notes: Time zone setting in Make scheduling is confirmed. The daylight saving time effect is standard time zone behavior and not Make-specific.

evidence.claim: Make scheduling allows time zone selection — confirmed in Make documentation.

diagnostic_signals: Scenario runs at a consistent but unexpected time (e.g., 2 hours earlier or later than expected)
The time offset corresponds to a time zone difference
The discrepancy changes during daylight saving time transitions
